title: En passant: capture a pawn in passing
outcomes: Captures en passant when told to, for White and for Black
Knows the capture must be made on the very next move
Says when en passant is not available

steps.text: **En passant** means 'in passing'. When an enemy pawn jumps two squares and lands right beside your pawn, you may capture it as if it had moved only one square. Your pawn goes to the square the enemy pawn passed over, and the enemy pawn is removed. You must do it on the very next move, or the chance is gone.

steps.caption: Black's pawn jumped from d7 to d5. White captures it as if it had stopped on d6.

line.say: The pawn captures en passant: it lands on d6 and the pawn on d5 is removed.

steps.title: Same pawns, one change
steps.prompt: Black has just jumped a pawn from d7 to d5, or it was standing on d5 already. Predict first: can White capture en passant?

steps.text: It works only on the move right after the two-square jump, and only for a pawn beside the jumper. If the enemy pawn arrived earlier, or by single steps, the right is gone; only the last move counts. Other pieces do not change the timing rule. (Like any move, the capture is not allowed if it would leave your own king in check; you meet that later.)

steps.prompt: Think of a game where a pawn of yours stood beside an enemy pawn. How would you check, before moving, that the enemy pawn had just jumped? Write the check as one question.
